AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 3, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL
MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION.
TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING, ATTEND THE MEETING IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS,
SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING:
(669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685 DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK
ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON
THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  5:30 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a)
  – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County Sheriff representative, and other related City
  officials.

  II.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54957: City Manager.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Properties: Various remnant parcels along the I-5 freeway located within the City; Agency
  Negotiator: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California Department of
  Transportation. Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Erasmus B. Soriano
  St. Linus Catholic Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Tatiana Valdovinos
  Youth Commissioner/Summer Youth Worker

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize August 7, 2021 as COVID-19 Awareness Day in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to recognize the 2021 Environmental Scholarship winners.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Summer Concert recap.

  3.  Street Projects update.
   4.  Chamber of Commerce Quarterly Report.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of July 20,
  2021. 825-04

  Report

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period June 27, 2021 – July 10,
  2021, in the total amount of $1,106,211.63. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period July
  15 - July 28, 2021, in the total amount of $7,598,495.82. 640

  Report

  5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Allstate
  Insurance (Albert Enrique) and Sylvia Hernandez. 830-01/08

  Report

  6.  PROJECT NO. 7925.1 - ACCEPTANCE OF WORK - LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION PROGRAM
  (CONCRETE IMPROVEMENTS) AT ZONE 27 (ENGINEERS REPORT NO. 21-17) – Staff
  recommends City Council accept the work of Kalban Inc. for $1,886,289.66 for Project No. 7925.1, the
  Local Street Rehabilitation Program (Concrete Improvements). 1005-04-7925.1

  Report

  7.  FISCAL YEAR 2021 JUSTICE ASSISTANCE GRANT – Staff recommends City Council approve the
  proposed Justice Assistance Grant submission allocating the 2021 funds for the purchase of equipment
  and to ensure compliance with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s National Incident-Based Reporting
  System; and designate the City Manager as the Chief Executive to complete grant related documents
  and amendments. 730-03-09

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  8.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  9.  ORDINANCE NO. 21-1727 – GRANTING A PIPELINE FRANCHISE TO TORRANCE PIPELINE
  COMPANY, LLC. – Staff recommends City Council introduce by title only Ordinance No. 21-1727, AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK GRANTING A PIPELINE FRANCHISE TO TORRANCE
  PIPELIINE COMPANY, LLC., and schedule for second reading. 618-03

  Report

REPORTS
   10. CONSIDERATION OF A CITY SPEED HUMP POLICY - Staff recommends City Council approve the
  proposed Speed Hump Policy and Pilot Program. 1050-09

  Report

  11. CONSIDERATION OF THE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT PROPOSED FUNDING ALLOCATIONS
  – Staff recommends City Council approve the American Rescue Plan Act $28 million Allocation Plan
  over a two-year period.

  Report

  12. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – AUGUST EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive
  and file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated July 30, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
